propositions: Inbound link removal permanently declines (guard G5) when a pair holds two differently-related net-active links and one relation's peer link vanishes, because removal is pair-scoped and returns only the most-recent link, creating a mismatch that never converges.

Write operations are relation-scoped (keyed on target_id, relation), allowing one ordered pair to hold multiple distinct relations simultaneously (blocks + relates_to), but removal operations are pair-scoped with no relation parameter, creating API asymmetry.

The outbound differ dedupes direction-agnostically on vendor type without deduping on relation, allowing same-vendor-type remote links in the other direction to prevent outbound re-adds that would normally suppress inbound removal records, causing removal records to reach G5 unhandled.

Removal must be made relation-scoped and symmetric with the write path: graph-layer remove_dependency seam keyed on (target_id, relation), optional relation parameter in CLI and library (backward-compatible with default None), and reconciler inbound removal using the relation-scoped removal to converge.
A removal naming a relation with no matching net-active local link must remove nothing (logged no-op), preserving the safety invariant that no link the peer still carries is ever destroyed.
The pair-scoped most-recent unlink behavior (rebar unlink id1 id2 with no relation argument) must remain byte-for-byte unchanged for backward compatibility.
